I think people who have accumulated enough ccp should be able to vote on subverses. The voting will work similar to the current ability to downvote, but will determine if the ccp from a certain subverse counts towards their ability to downvote in other places. That way subverses like that could be phased out and prove to be counter-productive, and would help prevent subverses like /v/shitvoaterssay being able to brigade in the ways they were allowed to on that other site.

This is an interesting idea, but here's something - even once you hit 100 CCP, it's not like you get unlimited upvoats and downvoats - you're still limited by a factor of your CCP.

Niche subverses, by definition, will have fewer users than larger, more popular ones. That means less CCP gained for the content there. So we're already weighting voats in favor of more popular subverses - if every person upvoats my contributions in a sub of 100 people, I'm still going to get a lot less CCP than if half the population of a sub of 1000 does. People that are valued contributors in big subs will naturally have more influence than those in smaller ones.

How much would a fully working n64 be worth nowadays?

I would estimate it around $60-$70 total with everything. Depends where you sell it though, obviously.

My local game store sells N64s with a controller for around $20 - $30 depending when you go in. The extra controller will probably fetch another $10 if they're both official N64 controllers.

Sports games are basically worthless, they sell for around $3 - $5 but the other two games you have are probably worth $10 - $15 each. They'd be worth a little more if you have the boxes in good condition but considering how damn flimsy the 64 boxes were I doubt many people do.
I would be astonished if people manage to keep the boxes after this long, but the cartridges are sturdy enough thtat they don't even need a box, unlike disks
Just check ebay, that would be the high end. If the controller's joysticks are in good shape, that's actually a big deal. Original N64 controllers with still tight joysticks go for a premium.
Really? One of them has a looser joystick but the other is still in great shape. I'm not planning on selling them or anything, just curious. Thanks :)

N64 joysticks are notorious for breaking down over time, particularly if people use them roughly (or played Mario Party 1 and rotated them around harshly a bunch). They sell replacement joysticks and they work, they just don't have the same exact feel the originals have, so a good tight original N64 joystick can go for like $30 (which is of course a lot for an old joystick).
